note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Lower bound of T^{-1/(2+p)} for uncoupled last-iterate learning with bandit feedback, matched by two algorithms

nodes.name: Average-iterate drawback
nodes.description: Regret-based methods for zero-sum matrix games produce policies that generally do not converge, and the average policy used as a proxy is hard to compute for practical (e.g. neural network) policies.

nodes.name: Prior bandit last-iterate rate
nodes.description: Prior work (Cai et al. 2023; Dong et al. 2024) obtained only O(T^{-1/8}) exploitability-gap rates for last-iterate convergence with bandit feedback, against a known lower bound of Omega(T^{-1/2}) from K-armed bandits.

nodes.name: Open question on the best rate
nodes.description: The best attainable rate for last-iterate convergence of uncoupled learning with bandit feedback in matrix games was an open question.

nodes.name: Lower bound for last-iterate convergence
nodes.description: For any p in (0,2], no uncoupled learning sequence with unobserved opponent actions can achieve Lp last-iterate convergence faster than T^{-1/(2+p)} on all 2x2 games, i.e. Omega(T^{-1/4}) for L2 (Theorem 5.1).

nodes.name: Intuition for the lower bound
nodes.description: In some 2x2 games a minimax policy makes all of the other player's actions equivalent so they cannot learn, while a policy converging to it only slows learning, so convergence to the minimax policy is detrimental to learning.

nodes.name: Lower bound extends to p>2
nodes.description: For p in (2,infinity], norm monotonicity yields the Omega(T^{-1/4}) lower bound for Lp last-iterate convergence (Corollary 5.3).

nodes.name: Last-iterate harder than average
nodes.description: Guaranteeing last-iterate convergence is strictly harder than average-iterate convergence, which attains O(T^{-1/2}).

nodes.name: Explore-or-exploit framework
nodes.description: Algorithm 1 uses a shared random seed to synchronize players, playing the current profile of an anytime algorithm A on exploration steps and its output on exploitation steps, with exploration probabilities p_t summing to infinity.

nodes.name: Framework rate lemma
nodes.description: If A has output convergence rate g, Algorithm 1 achieves an Lp last-iterate rate f_t built from p_t and g (Lemma 6.1).

nodes.name: Lower bound is tight for p<=2
nodes.description: Using EXP3-IX with p_t = t^{-p/(2+p)}, Algorithm 1 attains Lp last-iterate rate O~(t^{-1/(2+p)}), matching the lower bound up to constant and log factors (Theorem 6.2).

nodes.name: Framework still needs averages and sync
nodes.description: The first algorithm still needs average-policy computation (since it relies on A's output) and requires synchronizing the two players, so it is not practical.

nodes.name: Regularized EXP3 algorithm
nodes.description: Algorithm 2 runs mirror descent steps on a KL-regularized game L_tau with an unbiased loss estimate (instead of IX estimation), requiring no average policy.

nodes.name: Regularized EXP3 achieves L2 rate
nodes.description: With tau = ((A+B)/T)^{1/4} sqrt(2/(log A + log B)) and eta_t = 2/(tau(t+1)), Algorithm 2's final output has ||EG||_2 of order ((A+B)/T)^{1/4} sqrt(log(AB)), i.e. optimal O(T^{-1/4}) (Theorem 7.2).

nodes.name: Regularization needs the horizon
nodes.description: The regularization in Algorithm 2 depends on the horizon T, so the rate is only guaranteed near the final output and not anytime.

nodes.name: Doubling trick restores anytime guarantee
nodes.description: Algorithm 3 (doubling trick with synchronized instances) gives an anytime L2 last-iterate bound of order ((A+B)/t)^{1/4} sqrt(log AB) log t, i.e. O~(T^{-1/4}) (Theorem 8.1).

nodes.name: Doubling still requires synchronization
nodes.description: Algorithm 3 shares the weakness of requiring the two players to synchronize which instance to play.

isolated_nodes.name: Uncoupled Regularized EXP3 rates in Table 1
isolated_nodes.description: Table 1 lists this paper's Simultaneous Explore or Exploit with Lp rate O~(T^{-1/(2+p)}) for p in (0,2] and Uncoupled Regularized EXP3 with L2 rate O~(T^{-1/4}).

isolated_nodes.name: Extensive-form extension
isolated_nodes.description: The two approaches could be adapted to extensive-form games with IXOMD and dilated Shannon entropy regularization, obtaining the same horizon dependence.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the open question to the new lower bound, then to the explore-exploit algorithm showing tightness, then to the more practical regularized algorithm and its doubling-trick extension.
